text:
sara: quick RFC follow-up — I'm trying a different tack: deferred coalescing + explicit queue watermarks to avoid thrash from tiny microbatches. wanted to surface tradeoffs and get alignment before i open a PR.

sara: problem: current continuous-batcher often emits lots of 1-2 token microbatches under bursty workloads, which spikes tps and increases GPU kernel churn. naive batching windows hurt p50 but help cost; we need something in between.

tim: curious — how is deferred coalescing different from current adaptive window? sounds similar to hysteresis we discussed.

sara: good q. adaptive window grows/shrinks purely by observed arrivals. deferred coalescing adds a short explicit delay for coalescing at ingress + a pair of watermarks (low/high) to gate when the queue will force immediate flushes vs hold slightly longer. idea is to reduce oscillation when arrival rate hovers around a boundary.

jyoti: what are the knobs you plan to expose? per-tenant? global?

sara: plan: three knobs: coalesce_delay_ms (soft delay), watermark_low_ms (if oldest request waited > low => prefer flush soon), watermark_high_ms (if oldest waited > high => immediate flush). expose per-queue and a global override for Dedicated tiers.

max: how do watermarks interact with fairness? e.g., a noisy tenant could hold queue open to favor its larger batches.

sara: we enforce per-tenant queue slices + per-tenant watermarks. also will add a max-hold-ms per-slice to prevent starvation. if a tenant tries to monopolize, admission controller will short-circuit to a smaller batch or preempt.

elaine: any perf numbers from traces? even rough sim results?

sara: ran a synthetic trace from last week's prod spike: baseline p50=16ms, p95=110ms, p99=420ms on g4; with deferred coalesce (delay=6ms, low=12ms, high=40ms) p50=18ms (+2ms), p95=95ms (-15ms), p99=310ms (-110ms). token cost reduced ~12% due to fewer microbatches.

tim: those p99 gains look promising. but watch long-tail for cold-starts. any impact on streaming/early-flush semantics?

sara: streaming kept intact because streaming bypasses coalesce if request sets streaming=true. early flush (client TTL) will still trigger immediate flush. this is purely for non-streaming text generation paths.

jyoti: what about interactions with KV cache / prefix caching? if we delay, we might lose cache hit locality for subsequent tokens from same session.

sara: noted. deferred delay is tiny (single-digit ms) — should not harm intra-request KV locality. bigger risk is cross-request locality when we hold requests that would have hit an existing cached prefix on GPU; we may add a heuristic that when incoming request matches a hot-prefix tag we bypass coalesce.

max: rollout plan? A/B or ramp?

sara: A/B on dedicated hosts first, then canary on hosted with 1% traffic, monitoring p50/p95/p99, token cost, GPU utilization, and queue-length histogram. kill switches: set coalesce_delay_ms=0 or set high=1 to revert to immediate flush.

elaine: tests to add?

sara: unit tests for watermark transitions, e2e perf harness with replayer traces, and integration test to ensure streaming and early-flush bypass still work. also add telemetry: per-queue hold-duration histograms, flush-reason tags (timer, watermark_low, watermark_high, early_flush, streaming, admission).

tim: can you sketch the minimal operator interface? i want to make sure console + API can control these at route-level.

sara: minimal API: routeConfig.batch.coalesce_delay_ms, batch.watermark_low_ms, batch.watermark_high_ms, batch.max_hold_ms, batch.bypass_prefix_tags (list). I'll send a proto diff.

jyoti: perf regression budget? we should cap p50 increase to +5ms for hosted standard tier.

sara: agreed. we'll gate rollout by that.

eng-bot: deploy planned: sara/deferred-coalesce -> canary 1% -> metrics check -> 10% -> 50% -> 100%. automated rollback on p99 increase > +5% for 10m.

max: minor nit — add a metric for "flush_count_by_reason" so we can correlate kernels launched vs token throughput.

sara: will add. i'll open the RFC follow-up PR today with config proto, short perf report, and the perf harness traces. thanks all for the quick take. :thumbsup:
